chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer Layth al-Muradi, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Utba, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever says ten times, before the sun rises and before it sets: “There is no god but Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He gives life and causes death, and He causes death and gives life, and He is Ever-Living and will not die. In His Hand is the goodness, and He is Able over all things,” it will be an expiation for his sins for that day.'

key_terms.بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ: In His Hand is the goodness (divine power)
key_terms.حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ: Ever-Living and will not die (divine attribute)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (core creedal declaration)
key_terms.لَهُ الْمُلْكُ: For Him is the Kingdom (divine sovereignty)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death (divine attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting 'La ilaha illallah' ten times morning and evening?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific dhikr to be recited ten times before sunrise and sunset, serving as an expiation (kaffarah) for the day's sins. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of consistent morning and evening remembrance to cleanse minor sins and maintain spiritual purity throughout the day.
